title: flutter_local_notifications
objectives: Understand flutter_local_notifications via a real-life analogy
Configure Android channels + iOS categories + timezone data
Schedule + repeat notifications; handle timezone changes
Handle taps + deep links across foreground / background / terminated

sections.markdown:
**Think of `flutter_local_notifications` as the sticky-note dispenser your app owns on the fridge — vs FCM which is the postal service.**

- **FCM** — SERVER pushes a message; the OS wakes your app + optionally shows.
- **Local notifications** — YOUR APP tells the OS 'please show this to the user at time T with this content.' No server, no network. Perfect for: reminders, workout timers, downloaded-content-ready alerts, foreground FCM display (FCM notifications don't auto-render while the app is in the foreground).

**Key concepts:**
- **Channels (Android 8+)** — group notifications by category (`orders`, `promos`, `chat`); user can mute per channel in Settings. Channel = immutable settings package (importance, sound, vibration).
- **Categories (iOS)** — set of interactive actions attached to a notification type.
- **Zoned scheduling** — timezone-aware; a 'daily 8 AM alarm' should follow the user across timezones.
- **Sound + priority + full-screen intent (Android)** — cross the lockscreen for alarm-style critical use.
- **Payload** — arbitrary string attached to a notification; parsed on tap.

**Why every consumer + productivity app installs it:** cheap engagement (reminders), essential UX plumbing (foreground FCM display, scheduled workouts), and legally required in some flows (medication reminders). The complexity is worth it: getting notifications right is a huge trust/retention win.

**`flutter_local_notifications`** wraps Android **NotificationManager + AlarmManager** + iOS **UNUserNotificationCenter**. Provides: initialize (icon, categories, tap callback), `show`, `zonedSchedule`, `periodicallyShow`, `cancel[All]`, channel management, notification action buttons, big-text/inbox/messaging styles, media / progress bars, iOS Interruption Levels, full-screen intent. Companion: `timezone` package for zoned scheduling.

## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Not creating channels on Android 8+.** No channel = notification silently doesn't show. Create in `initialize`, not lazily.
**Mistake 2: Skipping Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS.** Runtime permission required; older devices auto-granted so devs forget.
**Mistake 3: Naive `Duration` arithmetic across timezones.** Doesn't handle DST + user relocation. Use `tz.TZDateTime` with the user's local timezone.
**Mistake 4: Missing background isolate handler.** Tap while app terminated → no callback → the deep link is lost. Register `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` background handler.
**Mistake 5: Non-idempotent IDs.** Reusing ID `1` for every notification overwrites the previous. Use `msg.hashCode` or a database sequence.
**Mistake 6: Ignoring channel importance.** Sound but muted = user pissed; too importance = spammy. Match to the category.

**Mistake 7: FCM notification message + local display combined = doubles.** If a FCM notification payload arrives while the app is background, the OS shows it AND `onBackgroundMessage` may re-show. Only display locally in `onMessage` (foreground).
**Mistake 8: Full-screen intent misuse.** Android reserves it for alarms + calls; misuse gets your app deprioritized by Google. Only use for genuine wake-me-up alarms.
## Best practices
**1. Channels per category** — `orders`, `chat`, `promos`, `reminders`. User controls per-channel mute.
**2. Android 13+ permission** on first launch after installation.
**3. Zoned scheduling with `tz.TZDateTime`** for reminders.
**4. Cancel + rebuild schedule** on timezone / DST change.
**5. Payload for deep linking** — JSON-encode a route + args.
**6. Background isolate handler** for terminated-tap navigation.
**7. Foreground FCM display via local_notifications** — the platform doesn't auto-show FCM in the foreground.
**8. Quiet hours + user preferences** — never send at 3 AM local.

## Interview Q&A

**Q1: FCM vs local notifications — when do you use each?**

**A:** **FCM** delivers messages from your SERVER at any time — remote push. Used for: chat messages, order updates, marketing campaigns triggered server-side, silent background sync. **Local notifications** are scheduled BY YOUR APP for the OS to display later without network. Used for: (1) local reminders (medication, workout, hydration); (2) downloaded-content-ready callbacks; (3) **displaying FCM notification payloads while the app is in the foreground** — because iOS + Android suppress the system-tray notification when the app is open. Typical app uses both: FCM for messages received from server, local for reminders + FCM foreground display. Interviewer red flag: 'local can replace FCM' — they can't (no network / cross-device sync); FCM alone can't schedule reliably.

**Q2: What are Android notification channels + why do they matter?**

**A:** Since Android 8 (Oreo), every notification MUST belong to a channel. Channel = immutable settings package: **name** (user-facing), **importance** (high / default / low / min), **sound**, **vibration**, **led color**, **badge**. **Users can mute per-channel** in system Settings — 'I want order updates but not promos.' **You define channels at first launch**; changing them afterwards has caveats (importance changes are ignored; user preferences win). **Best practice:** define categories users will care about (`orders`, `chat`, `promos`, `reminders`, `sync`); NEVER put everything in one 'default' channel. **Channel groups** — group related channels under a heading. **Notification without a channel on Android 8+ = silent-drop.** Interviewer bonus: knowing users can delete their notification history + per-channel muting is a differentiator.

**Q3: How do you deep-link from a notification tap in all three app states?**

**A:** **Foreground:** `onDidReceiveNotificationResponse` fires. Parse `resp.payload`, use your router (GoRouter / Navigator) to navigate. **Background (app suspended):** same callback fires because the isolate is warm. **Terminated (app killed):** register `onDidReceiveBackgroundNotificationResponse` — a **top-level `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` function** that runs in a background isolate. It can't touch the running UI (no BuildContext). Instead: persist the pending deep-link via `shared_preferences` (or a Hive box). On next foreground start of main isolate, read + navigate. **Alternative:** `getNotificationAppLaunchDetails()` in `main()` — returns the notification response if the app was launched from a tap. Combine both paths so no tap is lost. **Modern router:** GoRouter's `redirect` handles the pending deep-link on startup.

**Q4: How do you schedule notifications that survive timezone changes + DST?**

**A:** Naive `Duration(hours: 24)` addition breaks when: (1) user flies from Bangalore to New York; the 8 AM daily reminder now fires at 3 AM. (2) Fall-back / spring-forward DST — off by an hour. **Solution:** `tz.TZDateTime(tz.local, y, m, d, 8, 0)` — a timezone-aware datetime; the OS re-computes on delivery. **`matchDateTimeComponents: DateTimeComponents.time`** — repeat daily at that wall-clock time in whichever timezone the device is in. **On timezone change:** listen via periodic check or platform events; if changed, `cancelAll` + rebuild the schedule. **Persist schedule metadata in DB** — not just the notification IDs. **DST edge:** on the fall-back night, an 8 AM reminder still fires at 8 AM local; OS handles. Interviewers love hearing about the traveler-user scenario + repeat DST awareness.

**Q5: What are iOS Interruption Levels + Android importance — how do you pick?**

**A:** **iOS Interruption Levels** (iOS 15+): `passive` (silent, appear in tray only), `active` (default sound + banner), `time-sensitive` (breaks through Focus modes — 'delivery arriving now'), `critical` (bypass silent switch, needs Apple entitlement — for emergency alerts only). **Android importance:** `IMPORTANCE_MIN`, `LOW`, `DEFAULT`, `HIGH`, `MAX` (max = full-screen intent — reserved for alarms). Match to user value: news alerts = default; chat = high; workout timer end = default; alarm-app snooze notification = max + full-screen intent. **Anti-pattern:** everything on HIGH — trains users to ignore. **Regulator hint:** critical alerts on iOS require Apple approval + a real emergency-services justification.

**Q6: How do you test notification behavior?**

**A:** **Unit tests** — mock the plugin via method-channel overrides; assert `show / schedule` was called with the right arguments. **Manual on device** — real system behavior. **`adb shell dumpsys notification`** on Android to inspect. **iOS Simulator** simulates most; APNs delivery isn't real (test on real device). **Integration tests** with `patrol` can drive the notification tray. **Edge cases to test:** (1) tap while foreground / background / terminated; (2) tap during a phone call / DND; (3) permission denied; (4) channel muted by user; (5) timezone change mid-schedule; (6) low-battery Doze mode delaying deliveries. **CI limitations:** notification delivery on emulators is flaky; skip flaky suites; use unit tests for logic + manual verification for delivery. Interviewers respect knowing these limits.

## Real-world usage

- **FCM foreground display** — every consumer app.
- **Reminders** — medication, workouts, hydration, water plants.
- **Content-ready** — offline download complete, print job done.
- **Alarm-style** — timers, focus sessions.
- **NOT ideal for** — real-time chat (use FCM); background data sync (use WorkManager).

## Advanced notes

- **`fullScreenIntent: true`** — Android alarm-style; reserved use.
- **`ongoing: true`** — non-swipable (music player, ongoing call).
- **Big-text / inbox / messaging styles** — rich formats.
- **Media styles** — play/pause/skip controls.
- **Progress notifications** — for uploads / downloads.
- **Notification actions with `RemoteInput`** — quick reply on Android; UNTextInputAction on iOS.
- **Grouped notifications (Android)** — group by key + summary.
- **`silent: true`** — no sound / vibration.
- **`autoCancel: false`** — persists after tap.
- **`showWhen: false`** — hide timestamp.
- **iOS Communication Notifications (iOS 15+)** — richer chat notifications with sender identity.
- **Notification importance changes on Android** — users can override; app changes IGNORED after first set.
